newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up on economy, mining bull run.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up on economy, mining bull run.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Tuesday, as enthusiasm for mining stocks continued to lift a market already bolstered by strong fundamentals in the Peruvian economy, brokers said.
They predicted the same trend for Wednesday.

Tuesday, the General Index rose 2.03 percent to 1,901.4 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 2.39 percent to 2,791.0 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close at 1330 local time (1830 GMT). In a total of 1,836 trades, volume was a modest 31.0 million soles ($11.7 million), brokers said.

Morococha rose 7.84 percent to 6.05 soles on volume of 62,151 shares, while Atacocha jumped 7.73 percent to 1.95 soles on volume of 1.5 milion shares. These two miners have led the sector's bull run all month but another polymetalic miner, Milpo, also jumped Tuesday, climbing 9.41 percent to 27.79 soles on volume of 106,000 shares.

"There is a good feel about the polymetallic companies since the strength of zinc prices can be coupled with the fact that there are foreign investments and joint ventures which are seeking new reserves," said Luis Cueva of local brokerage Argos.
The mining sector was set to benefit from the country's improving economy, which has seen strong growth and decelerating inflation this year, brokers said.

The healthy economy meant benchmark Telefonica del Peru edged up Tuesday 0.16 percent, closing at 6.31 soles on improved volume of 1.0 million shares, and electricity distributor Luz del Sur closed up 0.33 percent at 3.00 soles on volume of 434,000 shares.
